1_1.title: Management Cybersecurity Training
1_1.description: Management takes part in cybersecurity training on a regular basis (§38(3) BSIG). The law sets no fixed interval; recommendation: every 3 years and whenever the management body changes.

1_4.title: Personal Liability Acknowledgment
1_4.description: Management confirms awareness of the liability rule in §38(2) BSIG (internal liability under company law). Not a statutory confirmation duty, but robust governance evidence for §38(1).

2_4.title: Risk Acceptance & IS Policy Sign-Off
2_4.description: Management signs the information security policy and accepts the residual risks from the risk register (2.3). The policy and the risk treatment plan must be reviewed at least annually and whenever significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks occur; the approval is renewed as part of that review (CIR 1.1.2, 2.1.4).

3_2.title: Detection, Classification & Logging
3_2.description: Set up a classification scheme (significant incident, §2 Nr. 11 BSIG), a reporting channel for suspicious events, detection processes and a complete incident log. Recurring incidents must be assessed on a quarterly basis (CIR 3.4.2(b)): incidents sharing the same apparent root cause that occur at least twice within six months and collectively meet the financial loss criterion count together as one significant incident (CIR Article 4).

3_3.title: BSI Reporting Readiness (24h/72h/1M)
3_3.description: Build the BSI reporting process: 24h early warning, 72h notification, intermediate report on BSI request, final report one month after the 72h notification (§32(1) BSIG). Set up reporting portal access and responsibilities. Reporting readiness is tested at planned intervals (CIR 3.5.5); no fixed interval is prescribed, recommendation: annually.

6_2.title: Secure Development & Configuration
6_2.description: Establish secure development guidelines (SDLC) and configuration baselines.

6_3.title: Vulnerability Management
6_3.description: Implement vulnerability management with scanning, risk-based prioritisation and a disclosure process; document deliberate non-remediation.

7_1.title: Security KPIs & Metrics
7_1.description: Define measurable security KPIs and report them at a self-set rhythm with trends and thresholds (recommendation: quarterly).

7_3.title: Management Review
7_3.description: Management reviews compliance with the policies and receives regular reporting on the state of information security (§30(2) Nr. 6, §38(1) BSIG, CIR 2.2.1). No fixed interval is prescribed; recommendation: an annual management review with gap analysis.

8_3.title: Role-Specific & Management Training
8_3.description: Specialised training for roles with security duties, including on role changes. Management training is evidenced under 1.1.

8_4.title: Training Effectiveness & Phishing Simulations
8_4.description: Measure the effectiveness of training and awareness (§30(2) Nr. 6 BSIG). Phishing simulations are an established method, not a legal duty; involve the works council and data protection first.

9_3.title: Key & Certificate Management
9_3.description: Document and implement key and certificate management across the full lifecycle (e.g. key vault or HSM where appropriate).

10_4.title: Access Reviews
10_4.description: Review and document access rights including privileged accounts on a regular basis. Legally: at planned intervals; recommendation: quarterly.

11_1.title: Authentication: where MFA is mandatory
11_1.description: Roll out MFA risk-based and document exceptions with compensating controls. Recommended order: admin accounts first, then internet-facing services, then the remaining systems.

11_3.title: Authentication Standards
11_3.description: Review authentication procedures and the password policy against current standards on a regular basis (NIST SP 800-63B, BSI IT-Grundschutz ORP.4).

12_3.title: Registration Maintenance
12_3.description: Report changes to registration data to the BSI without delay, at the latest within two weeks (§33(5) BSIG); additionally verify the data annually and keep the contact person reachable.

12_4.title: Compliance Evidence
12_4.description: Maintain documentation of implementation on an ongoing basis (§30(1) S. 3 BSIG). Only for operators of critical facilities: evidence every 3 years (§39) and attack detection (§31(2)); special registration under §34 only for the entity types of §60(1) BSIG.

G-DPA_1.title: Data Processing Agreements
G-DPA_1.description: Maintain a register of every processor that handles personal data on your behalf, with a signed DPA covering the eight Art. 28(3) clauses.

G-DPA_2.title: Sub-processor Authorisation
G-DPA_2.description: Track each processor's sub-processors and confirm prior authorisation per Art. 28(2)/(4).

G-ROP_1.title: Records of Processing Activities
G-ROP_1.description: Record each processing activity with the seven Art. 30(1) entries: controller and DPO contacts, purposes, categories of data subjects and of personal data, recipient categories, third-country transfers with safeguards and, where possible, erasure periods and a description of the measures.

G-TOM_1.title: Technical and Organisational Measures
G-TOM_1.description: Document the measures protecting personal data: pseudonymisation and encryption, lasting confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience, timely restoration after an incident, and a process for regularly testing and evaluating their effectiveness (Art. 32(1)).

G-BRC_1.title: Personal Data Breach Response Process
G-BRC_1.description: Establish written procedure for assessing and notifying the supervisory authority of personal data breaches within 72 hours (Art. 33).

G-BRC_2.title: Personal Data Breach Documentation
G-BRC_2.description: Internally document every personal data breach (notifiable or not) for supervisory-authority verification (Art. 33(5)).

G-DSR_1.title: Data Subject Rights Workflow
G-DSR_1.description: Process for handling access, erasure, rectification, portability, restriction, and objection requests within one month (Art. 12-22).

IS-4_1.title: Context of the Organization
IS-4_1.description: Determine external and internal issues relevant to the ISMS purpose and that affect your ability to achieve intended outcomes.

IS-4_2.title: Needs of Interested Parties
IS-4_2.description: Identify interested parties (customers, regulators, staff, suppliers) and their requirements relevant to information security.

IS-4_3.title: ISMS Scope
IS-4_3.description: Define and document the boundaries of the ISMS: which systems, locations, and activities are included and excluded, and why.

IS-4_4.title: Information Security Management System
IS-4_4.description: Establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve an ISMS in accordance with ISO 27001 requirements.

IS-5_1.title: Leadership and Commitment
IS-5_1.description: Top management must demonstrate commitment: approve the IS policy, ensure ISMS resources, and integrate security into business processes.

IS-5_2.title: Information Security Policy
IS-5_2.description: Establish, document, and communicate an IS policy signed by top management, including objectives and commitment to continual improvement.

IS-5_3.title: Roles, Responsibilities and Authorities
IS-5_3.description: Assign and communicate responsibilities for information security roles including CISO/ISMS owner, asset owners, and process owners.

IS-6_1.title: Risk Assessment Process
IS-6_1.description: Define and apply a documented risk assessment methodology including risk identification, analysis, evaluation, and acceptance criteria.

IS-6_2.title: Information Security Objectives
IS-6_2.description: Establish measurable IS objectives aligned to the IS policy, document plans to achieve them, and track progress.

IS-6_3.title: Planning of Changes
IS-6_3.description: When changes to the ISMS are needed, plan them in a controlled manner: assess purpose, consequences, integrity, resources, and accountability.

IS-7_1.title: Resources
IS-7_1.description: Determine and provide the resources needed to establish, implement, maintain, and continually improve the ISMS.

IS-7_2.title: Competence
IS-7_2.description: Determine competence requirements for ISMS-relevant roles, provide training, and retain evidence of competence (training records, certificates).

IS-7_3.title: Awareness
IS-7_3.description: Ensure persons doing work under the organization's control are aware of the IS policy, their contribution to ISMS effectiveness, and the implications of non-conformity.

IS-7_4.title: Communication
IS-7_4.description: Determine the internal and external communications relevant to the ISMS: what, when, with whom, how, and by whom.

IS-7_5.title: Documented Information
IS-7_5.description: Create and maintain documented information required by ISO 27001, and control its creation, update, distribution, and retention.

IS-8_1.title: Operational Planning and Control
IS-8_1.description: Plan, implement, and control the processes needed to meet IS requirements and implement the actions determined in Clause 6.

IS-8_2.title: Information Security Risk Assessment
IS-8_2.description: Perform risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes occur; document results in a risk register.

IS-8_3.title: Information Security Risk Treatment
IS-8_3.description: Select and implement risk treatment options; produce a risk treatment plan and Statement of Applicability (SoA).

IS-9_1.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis and Evaluation
IS-9_1.description: Define what to monitor and measure, how, when, and by whom; analyse and evaluate results against IS objectives.

IS-9_2.title: Internal Audit
IS-9_2.description: Conduct internal audits at planned intervals to assess whether the ISMS conforms to requirements and is effectively implemented.

IS-9_3.title: Management Review
IS-9_3.description: Top management reviews the ISMS at planned intervals covering audit results, KPIs, incidents, changes, and improvement opportunities.

IS-10_1.title: Continual Improvement
IS-10_1.description: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the ISMS.

IS-10_2.title: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
IS-10_2.description: When nonconformity occurs: react, investigate root cause, implement corrective action, and verify its effectiveness.

A_5_1.title: Policies for Information Security
A_5_1.description: Define, approve, publish, and annually review information security policies covering all relevant topics.

A_5_2.title: Information Security Roles and Responsibilities
A_5_2.description: Assign and document roles and responsibilities for information security across the organization.

A_5_3.title: Segregation of Duties
A_5_3.description: Separate conflicting duties and responsibilities to reduce opportunities for unauthorized modification of information.

A_5_4.title: Management Responsibilities
A_5_4.description: Management must require all personnel to apply information security in accordance with established policies.

A_5_5.title: Contact with Authorities
A_5_5.description: Maintain appropriate contacts with relevant authorities (data protection authority, cybersecurity agency, law enforcement).

A_5_6.title: Contact with Special Interest Groups
A_5_6.description: Maintain membership or contact with special interest groups, security forums, and professional associations.

A_5_7.title: Threat Intelligence
A_5_7.description: Collect, analyse, and produce threat intelligence relevant to the organization to anticipate and prepare for threats.

A_5_8.title: Information Security in Project Management
A_5_8.description: Integrate information security into project management to ensure security risks are addressed during projects.

A_5_9.title: Inventory of Information and Other Associated Assets
A_5_9.description: Identify, document, and maintain an inventory of information and associated assets with assigned ownership.

A_5_10.title: Acceptable Use of Information and Other Associated Assets
A_5_10.description: Identify, document, and implement acceptable use rules for information and assets, covering devices, data handling, and prohibited activities.

A_5_11.title: Return of Assets
A_5_11.description: Ensure all assets are returned upon termination or change of employment or contract.

A_5_12.title: Classification of Information
A_5_12.description: Classify information by sensitivity (confidential, internal, public) to ensure appropriate handling and protection.

A_5_13.title: Labelling of Information
A_5_13.description: Develop and implement a labelling procedure for information in accordance with the classification scheme.

A_5_14.title: Information Transfer
A_5_14.description: Establish rules and procedures for information transfer via all channels including email, messaging, physical media, and verbal.

A_5_15.title: Access Control
A_5_15.description: Define and implement access control rules based on business and security requirements, using least privilege.

A_5_16.title: Identity Management
A_5_16.description: Manage the full identity lifecycle (provisioning, changes, revocation) for all users and service accounts.

A_5_17.title: Authentication Information
A_5_17.description: Manage authentication information (passwords, keys, tokens) through a formal process including allocation, storage, and revocation.

A_5_18.title: Access Rights
A_5_18.description: Provision, review, modify, and remove access rights in accordance with the access control policy.

A_5_19.title: Information Security in Supplier Relationships
A_5_19.description: Identify and implement controls to protect assets accessible to suppliers; document requirements in supplier agreements.

A_5_20.title: Addressing Information Security Within Supplier Agreements
A_5_20.description: Establish and agree information security requirements with each supplier that may access, process, or store organizational information.

A_5_21.title: Managing Information Security in the ICT Supply Chain
A_5_21.description: Define and implement processes for managing information security risks associated with ICT products and services supply chain.

A_5_22.title: Monitoring, Review and Change Management of Supplier Services
A_5_22.description: Regularly monitor, review, and manage changes to supplier information security practices and service delivery.

A_5_23.title: Information Security for Use of Cloud Services
A_5_23.description: Establish processes for acquiring, using, managing, and exiting from cloud services, including security requirements and exit plans.

A_5_24.title: Information Security Incident Management Planning and Preparation
A_5_24.description: Plan and prepare for incident management with defined roles, responsibilities, procedures, and communication channels.

A_5_25.title: Assessment and Decision on Information Security Events
A_5_25.description: Assess information security events and decide whether they qualify as incidents using a defined classification scheme.

A_5_26.title: Response to Information Security Incidents
A_5_26.description: Respond to incidents in accordance with documented procedures; contain, eradicate, and recover in a structured way.

A_5_27.title: Learning from Information Security Incidents
A_5_27.description: Use knowledge from incidents to reduce the likelihood and impact of future incidents; update controls accordingly.

A_5_28.title: Collection of Evidence
A_5_28.description: Define and apply procedures for identifying, collecting, acquiring, and preserving evidence of information security incidents.

A_5_29.title: Information Security During Disruption
A_5_29.description: Plan how information security will be maintained during disruption. Integrate security requirements into business continuity plans.

A_5_30.title: ICT Readiness for Business Continuity
A_5_30.description: Plan, implement, maintain, and test ICT readiness based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.

A_5_31.title: Legal, Statutory, Regulatory and Contractual Requirements
A_5_31.description: Identify, document, and keep current all legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to information security.

A_5_32.title: Intellectual Property Rights
A_5_32.description: Implement procedures to protect intellectual property rights and comply with software licensing requirements.

A_5_33.title: Protection of Records
A_5_33.description: Protect records from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access, and unauthorized release in accordance with legal requirements.

A_5_34.title: Privacy and Protection of PII
A_5_34.description: Identify and meet privacy and personal data protection requirements in accordance with applicable law (GDPR).

A_5_35.title: Independent Review of Information Security
A_5_35.description: Review the ISMS approach and implementation independently at planned intervals or when significant changes occur.

A_5_36.title: Compliance with Policies, Rules and Standards for Information Security
A_5_36.description: Regularly review compliance with information security policies, standards, and procedures; document results.

A_5_37.title: Documented Operating Procedures
A_5_37.description: Document, maintain, and make available operating procedures for information processing facilities.

A_6_1.title: Screening
A_6_1.description: Perform background verification checks on all candidates for employment, proportionate to role sensitivity and legal requirements.

A_6_2.title: Terms and Conditions of Employment
A_6_2.description: Contractually require employees and contractors to comply with information security policies as a condition of employment.

A_6_3.title: Information Security Awareness, Education and Training
A_6_3.description: Ensure all staff receive appropriate security awareness training at hire and annually, with role-specific training for technical staff.

A_6_4.title: Disciplinary Process
A_6_4.description: Have a formal, communicated disciplinary process for employees who commit information security violations.

A_6_5.title: Responsibilities After Termination or Change of Employment
A_6_5.description: Define and enforce information security responsibilities that remain in effect after employment ends (confidentiality, asset return).

A_6_6.title: Confidentiality or Non-Disclosure Agreements
A_6_6.description: Identify, document, and regularly review confidentiality requirements; use NDAs with staff, contractors, and relevant third parties.

A_6_7.title: Remote Working
A_6_7.description: Define and implement security measures for remote working covering network security, physical security, and equipment protection.

A_6_8.title: Information Security Event Reporting
A_6_8.description: Provide a clear, easy-to-use mechanism for staff to report security events and weaknesses; act on all reports.

A_7_1.title: Physical Security Perimeters
A_7_1.description: Define and implement physical security perimeters to protect sensitive areas containing information and processing facilities.

A_7_2.title: Physical Entry
A_7_2.description: Protect secure areas with appropriate entry controls to ensure only authorized persons can gain access.

A_7_3.title: Securing Offices, Rooms and Facilities
A_7_3.description: Apply physical security to offices, rooms, and facilities proportionate to the sensitivity of the information processed there.

A_7_4.title: Physical Security Monitoring
A_7_4.description: Monitor premises for unauthorized physical access using alarms, CCTV, guards, or other appropriate means.

A_7_5.title: Protecting Against Physical and Environmental Threats
A_7_5.description: Protect against physical and environmental threats such as fire, flood, earthquake, and deliberate damage.

A_7_6.title: Working in Secure Areas
A_7_6.description: Define and apply procedures for working in secure areas to prevent unauthorized access, photography, or data exfiltration.

A_7_7.title: Clear Desk and Clear Screen
A_7_7.description: Apply a clear desk policy for papers and removable media, and a clear screen policy for information processing facilities.

A_7_8.title: Equipment Siting and Protection
A_7_8.description: Site and protect equipment to reduce risks from environmental threats, unauthorized access, and interference.

A_7_9.title: Security of Assets Off-Premises
A_7_9.description: Apply controls to assets taken off-premises, proportionate to the risks of working outside the organization's premises.

A_7_10.title: Storage Media
A_7_10.description: Manage storage media throughout its lifecycle: acquisition, use, transportation, disposal, and sanitization.

A_7_11.title: Supporting Utilities
A_7_11.description: Protect information processing facilities from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities.

A_7_12.title: Cabling Security
A_7_12.description: Protect power and telecommunications cabling from interception, interference, or damage.

A_7_13.title: Equipment Maintenance
A_7_13.description: Maintain equipment correctly to ensure continued availability and integrity of information processing facilities.

A_7_14.title: Secure Disposal or Re-Use of Equipment
A_7_14.description: Verify that all sensitive data and licensed software has been removed or overwritten prior to disposal or re-use of equipment.

A_8_1.title: User Endpoint Devices
A_8_1.description: Protect information on and processed by user endpoint devices (laptops, phones) using an endpoint security policy.

A_8_2.title: Privileged Access Rights
A_8_2.description: Restrict and carefully manage the allocation and use of privileged access rights across all systems.

A_8_3.title: Information Access Restriction
A_8_3.description: Restrict access to information and systems to what is required for each user's role, using least privilege.

A_8_4.title: Access to Source Code
A_8_4.description: Restrict access to program source code and associated tools to authorized persons only; apply version control.

A_8_5.title: Secure Authentication
A_8_5.description: Implement secure authentication technologies and procedures including MFA for sensitive systems and all remote access.

A_8_6.title: Capacity Management
A_8_6.description: Monitor and adjust resource usage and projections to ensure required system capacity and performance.

A_8_7.title: Protection Against Malware
A_8_7.description: Implement malware protection controls (EDR, AV, code signing, email filtering) supported by appropriate user awareness.

A_8_8.title: Management of Technical Vulnerabilities
A_8_8.description: Timely identification, evaluation, and remediation of technical vulnerabilities across all systems.

A_8_9.title: Configuration Management
A_8_9.description: Establish, document, and maintain configurations (including security configurations) for hardware, software, and cloud services.

A_8_10.title: Information Deletion
A_8_10.description: Delete information when it is no longer required, in accordance with legal, contractual, and business requirements.

A_8_11.title: Data Masking
A_8_11.description: Use data masking, pseudonymization, or anonymization to protect personal data in non-production environments.

A_8_12.title: Data Leakage Prevention
A_8_12.description: Apply data leakage prevention measures to systems, networks, and endpoints that process sensitive information.

A_8_13.title: Information Backup
A_8_13.description: Make and regularly test backup copies of information, software, and system images in accordance with an agreed backup policy.

A_8_14.title: Redundancy of Information Processing Facilities
A_8_14.description: Implement sufficient redundancy in information processing facilities to meet availability requirements.

A_8_15.title: Logging
A_8_15.description: Produce, protect, and retain logs of user activities, exceptions, faults, and security events for defined retention periods.

A_8_16.title: Monitoring Activities
A_8_16.description: Monitor networks, systems, and applications to detect anomalous behaviour and potential security events.

A_8_17.title: Clock Synchronization
A_8_17.description: Synchronize clocks of all information processing systems to an approved time source to support log correlation and forensics.

A_8_18.title: Use of Privileged Utility Programs
A_8_18.description: Control and restrict the use of utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls.

A_8_19.title: Installation of Software on Operational Systems
A_8_19.description: Implement procedures to control software installation on operational systems by authorized persons only.

A_8_20.title: Networks Security
A_8_20.description: Secure networks and network devices to protect information in systems and applications.

A_8_21.title: Security of Network Services
A_8_21.description: Identify, implement, and monitor security mechanisms for network services, including cloud networking.

A_8_22.title: Segregation of Networks
A_8_22.description: Segregate groups of information services, users, and information systems within the network.

A_8_23.title: Web Filtering
A_8_23.description: Manage access to external websites to reduce exposure to malicious content.

A_8_24.title: Use of Cryptography
A_8_24.description: Define and implement a cryptography policy covering approved algorithms, key management, and encryption requirements.

A_8_25.title: Secure Development Life Cycle
A_8_25.description: Establish and apply rules for the secure development of software and systems throughout the development lifecycle.

A_8_26.title: Application Security Requirements
A_8_26.description: Identify, specify, and approve information security requirements for application development and procurement.

A_8_27.title: Secure System Architecture and Engineering Principles
A_8_27.description: Establish, document, and apply secure engineering principles for all development and system engineering activities.

A_8_28.title: Secure Coding
A_8_28.description: Apply secure coding principles to software development to prevent common vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10, injection, XSS).

A_8_29.title: Security Testing in Development and Acceptance
A_8_29.description: Define and implement security testing processes in the development lifecycle and during acceptance testing.

A_8_30.title: Outsourced Development
A_8_30.description: Supervise and monitor outsourced system development activities to ensure security requirements are met.

A_8_31.title: Separation of Development, Test and Production Environments
A_8_31.description: Separate development, testing, and production environments to reduce the risk of unauthorized access or changes to the production system.

A_8_32.title: Change Management
A_8_32.description: Manage changes to information processing facilities and systems through a formal change management process.

A_8_33.title: Test Information
A_8_33.description: Protect and manage test information; never use live production data in test environments without appropriate controls.

A_8_34.title: Protection of Information Systems During Audit Testing
A_8_34.description: Plan and agree audit requirements and activities involving verification of operational systems to minimize disruption.

AI-LIT_1.title: AI Literacy
AI-LIT_1.description: Ensure staff who operate or use AI systems have a sufficient level of AI literacy (AI Act Art. 4).

AI-LIT_2.title: Deployer AI Literacy
AI-LIT_2.description: Brief management and deployers on their AI Act obligations and confirm the literacy programme (Art. 4, Art. 26(2)).

AI-PRO_1.title: Prohibited Practices Policy
AI-PRO_1.description: Document a policy that bans the AI practices prohibited under AI Act Art. 5(1)(a) to (i).

AI-PRO_2.title: No Prohibited AI in Use
AI-PRO_2.description: Provide evidence that no prohibited AI practice is deployed in the organisation (Art. 5).

AI-INV_1.title: AI System Inventory
AI-INV_1.description: Maintain an inventory of AI systems with their risk classification under AI Act Art. 6 and Art. 26.

AI-INV_2.title: High-Risk Classification
AI-INV_2.description: Record the high-risk classification and applicability for each AI system (Art. 6, Art. 50).

AI-INV_3.title: Provider or Deployer Role
AI-INV_3.description: Determine and document whether you act as provider or deployer for each AI system (Art. 25).

AI-RSK_1.title: AI Risk Management System
AI-RSK_1.description: Establish a risk management system for high-risk AI systems across their lifecycle (AI Act Art. 9).

AI-RSK_2.title: AI Risk Review
AI-RSK_2.description: Review and update the AI risk management system on a regular basis (Art. 9).

AI-FRI_1.title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
AI-FRI_1.description: Carry out and sign off a fundamental rights impact assessment for the relevant high-risk AI systems (AI Act Art. 27).

AI-OVS_1.title: Human Oversight Measures
AI-OVS_1.description: Implement human oversight measures for high-risk AI systems in operation (Art. 14, Art. 26(2)).

AI-OVS_2.title: Human Oversight Review
AI-OVS_2.description: Review whether human oversight measures remain effective (Art. 14).

AI-TRA_1.title: AI Interaction Disclosure
AI-TRA_1.description: Inform people when they interact with an AI system, unless it is obvious (AI Act Art. 50(1)).

AI-TRA_2.title: Marking Synthetic Content
AI-TRA_2.description: Mark AI-generated or manipulated audio, image, video and text in a machine-readable way (Art. 50(2)).

AI-TRA_3.title: Deepfake and Emotion Disclosure
AI-TRA_3.description: Disclose deepfakes and emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation use to affected persons (Art. 50(4)).

AI-INC_1.title: Serious Incident Reporting Policy
AI-INC_1.description: Define a procedure for reporting serious AI incidents to the authorities (AI Act Art. 73).

AI-INC_2.title: Serious Incident Notification
AI-INC_2.description: Report serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems within the AI Act deadlines (Art. 73).

AI-DOC_1.title: AI Technical Documentation
AI-DOC_1.description: Prepare and maintain technical documentation per AI Act Annex IV (Art. 11, Art. 18).

AI-DOC_2.title: Automatic Logging
AI-DOC_2.description: Enable and retain automatic event logs generated by high-risk AI systems (Art. 12, Art. 19).

AI-DOC_3.title: EU Declaration of Conformity
AI-DOC_3.description: Draw up and sign the EU declaration of conformity for high-risk AI systems (Art. 47, Annex V).

AI-GPI_1.title: GPAI Technical Documentation
AI-GPI_1.description: Maintain technical documentation for general-purpose AI models (AI Act Art. 53(1)(a)).

AI-GPI_2.title: GPAI Copyright Policy
AI-GPI_2.description: Put in place a policy to comply with EU copyright law for GPAI training (Art. 53(1)(c)).

AI-GPI_3.title: GPAI Training Data Summary
AI-GPI_3.description: Publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used to train the GPAI model (Art. 53(1)(d)).

AI-GPI_4.title: GPAI Systemic Risk Obligations
AI-GPI_4.description: Meet the additional obligations for GPAI models with systemic risk (AI Act Art. 55).

CRA-MFG_1.title: Product Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
CRA-MFG_1.description: Perform a cybersecurity risk assessment for the product with digital elements (CRA Art. 13(2)).

CRA-MFG_2.title: Manufacturer Due Diligence
CRA-MFG_2.description: Confirm manufacturer due diligence so products meet the essential requirements (Art. 13(1)).

CRA-ESS_1.title: Secure-by-Design Requirements
CRA-ESS_1.description: Design and produce products to meet the essential cybersecurity requirements (CRA Annex I Part I).

CRA-ESS_2.title: Secure Default Configuration
CRA-ESS_2.description: Ship products with a secure-by-default configuration (Annex I Part I, point 3(a)).

CRA-ESS_3.title: No Known Exploitable Vulnerabilities
CRA-ESS_3.description: Place products on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities (Annex I Part I, point 1).

CRA-VLN_1.title: Vulnerability Handling Policy
CRA-VLN_1.description: Establish a process to identify, document and remediate vulnerabilities (CRA Annex I Part II, points 1 to 2).

CRA-VLN_2.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
CRA-VLN_2.description: Adopt a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy with a contact address (Annex I Part II, point 5).

CRA-VLN_3.title: Security Update Delivery
CRA-VLN_3.description: Provide security updates without delay and free of charge during the support period (Annex I Part II, point 3).

CRA-VLN_4.title: Vulnerability Testing
CRA-VLN_4.description: Test and review the security of the product on a regular basis (Annex I Part II, point 8).

CRA-INC_1.title: Early Warning Notification
CRA-INC_1.description: Send an early warning of an actively exploited vulnerability to the CSIRT and ENISA (CRA Art. 14(2)(a)).

CRA-INC_2.title: Vulnerability Notification
CRA-INC_2.description: Notify the vulnerability or severe incident within the CRA deadline (Art. 14(2)(b)).

CRA-INC_3.title: Final Incident Report
CRA-INC_3.description: Submit the final report on the vulnerability or incident to the authorities (Art. 14(2)(c)).

CRA-INC_4.title: User Notification
CRA-INC_4.description: Inform affected users of the incident and any corrective measures (Art. 14(4)).

CRA-CONF_1.title: Conformity Assessment
CRA-CONF_1.description: Carry out the applicable conformity assessment procedure for the product (CRA Art. 24).

CRA-CONF_2.title: CE Marking and Conformity
CRA-CONF_2.description: Affix the CE marking and draw up the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 27).

CRA-DOC_1.title: CRA Technical Documentation
CRA-DOC_1.description: Compile and keep up to date the technical documentation per CRA Annex VII (Art. 28).

CRA-SUP_1.title: Support Period
CRA-SUP_1.description: Determine and sign off the support period during which security updates are provided (CRA Art. 13(8)).

CRA-SBOM_1.title: Software Bill of Materials
CRA-SBOM_1.description: Produce a software bill of materials covering the top-level dependencies (CRA Annex I Part II, point 1).

CRA-IMP_1.title: Importer Obligations
CRA-IMP_1.description: Verify that imported products meet CRA requirements before placing them on the market (Art. 18).

CRA-IMP_2.title: Distributor Obligations
CRA-IMP_2.description: Check CRA conformity and act on non-conformity when distributing products (Art. 19).

CRA-OSS_1.title: Open-Source Steward Duties
CRA-OSS_1.description: Document the cybersecurity policy expected of open-source software stewards (CRA Art. 24).
